text: Writing clean code is important for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, which helps you and others work with it. First, use clear naming conventions for variables and functions. A name like "totalPrice" is much better than "tp". Second, keep your functions small and focused. Each function should do one job well. This makes your code easier to test and fix. Finally, remember that clean code is easier to maintain. When you need to change something later, you will save time and avoid mistakes. Writing clean code takes practice, but it is a valuable skill.
